land.text: Arakan, taken when the Burmese 'captured the Arakanese capital, Mrauk-U, on January 2, 1785'

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Mrauk U shapes to 1787 and gives Arakan to the Konbaung shape from 1788; the pages date the conquest to 31 December 1784-2 January 1785.

capitals.name: Launggyet
capitals.note: Infobox: Launggyet 1429-1430. Coordinates approximate ('southeast of Mrauk U', Konbaung conquest page); no page opened gives them.

capitals.name: Mrauk-U (Mrohaung)
capitals.note: Infobox: Mrauk U 1430-1785; the body says 'declared the capital of the Arakanese kingdom in 1431'. Min Saw Mon page: founded 16 November 1430, 'completed in 1432/33' and moved to then.

keyframe_review.note: 84,574 km2 (281 cells, Rakhine, Chin Hills and Magwe edge). The Mrauk U page gives no area (only that Razagyi's territory 'nearly doubled'), so no ratio. The Min Saw Mon page says his domain 'was still restricted to northern Arakan' while Sandoway stayed independent, and the Mrauk U page has Min Khayi 'annexed Sandoway and Ramu in 1437': the shape holds in full only from 1437, so for 1429-1436 Sandoway (28 of the 281 cells) comes off.

correction.text: northern Arakan from Launggyet, Sandoway not yet annexed (applies 1429-1436 only)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1437-1458: Cliopatria's 1429 outline (Sandoway now inside) with Ramu, south of Chittagong in modern Bangladesh. 'Min Khayi annexed Sandoway and Ramu in 1437.' Cliopatria's shapes have nothing in Bangladesh until 1534.

correction.text: the Arakan coast with Sandoway and Ramu, annexed in 1437

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1459-1481: the 1534 outline (Chittagong inside). The Mrauk U infobox gives 'Conquest of Chittagong: 1459'; the Bengal Sultanate page has 'A war with Arakan in 1459 led to the defeat of Bengali Sultan Rukunuddin Barbak Shah' and 'During the reign of Rukunuddin Barbak Shah, the Kingdom of Mrauk U conquered Chittagong' (no year). The Mrauk U body credits Ba Saw Phyu without a year, and the Min Bin page has Chittagong taken again in 1532, so this hold is lost in between (ledger 1516).

union.text: Chittagong and the hills above it (the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1534)

correction.text: the Arakan coast with Chittagong, conquered in 1459 (infobox)

keyframe_review.note: 84,395 km2: four cells fewer than 1429-1481 on the Ava edge (lon 94.4-94.9), the year Ava's shape also changes; the pages say nothing about that frontier. Chittagong and Ramu stay in until the Bengal war of 1512-1516 ('Hussain Shah restored Bengali sovereignty in Chittagong and northern Arakan after the war of 1512-1516'), so the corrected shape for 1482-1515 adds them; the outline then comes out in 1516 (next keyframe).

union.text: Chittagong and the hills above it (the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1534)

correction.text: the 1482 outline with Chittagong and Ramu (applies 1482-1515 only)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1516-1528: the 1482 outline with Ramu, without Chittagong, which Bengal recovered in the war of 1512-1516. The Bengal page also says Hussain Shah restored sovereignty in 'northern Arakan'; no other page supports a Bengali hold on Arakan proper (Min Bin's 1531 coronation, the 1530s walls of Mrauk-U), so only Chittagong is taken off.

84,425 km2: the same outline as 1482-1528. It is right for 1529-1531 (with Ramu); Chittagong returns in October 1532 ('defeated a Bengal army of 10,000 men and took Chittagong'), so the 1529 shape applies to 1529-1531 only. The Mrauk U lead says a protectorate of Bengal 'from 1429 to 1531'; Min Bin was crowned 16 September 1531.

correction.text: the Arakan coast without Chittagong (applies 1529-1531 only)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1532-1533: Chittagong retaken in October 1532, so the 1534 outline begins two years early. The invasion began 7 October 1532; Dhaka was entered on 11 December 1532 and left on 13 April 1533 (ledger), but 'his control of Bengal beyond Chittagong was largely nominal'.

102,177 km2 (332 cells): Arakan with Chittagong. The Mrauk U page says Min Bin seized Chittagong in the late 1530s and a 1542 inscription shows rule 'firmly established' by the 1540s; the Min Bin page dates it 1532 (used). Tripuri raids on Chittagong and Ramu continued but did not move the border. The 1545-47 Toungoo invasion is a ledger occupation of Thandwe.

52,360 km2: Cliopatria cuts 159 cells (Rakhine south of the Lemro, Chin and Magwe edge) to the Toungoo shape for 1547-1551. The Min Bin page has the Toungoo siege of Mrauk-U fail (truce 30 January 1547, retreat 2 February, 'Toungoo evacuated Thandwe' on 26 March 1547) and the Mrauk U page that Mrauk U 'successfully repelled the Toungoo invasions' by 1547. Replace by the 1534 outline.

correction.text: the 1534 outline kept for 1547-1551: Toungoo withdrew from Thandwe on 26 March 1547

keyframe_review.note: 100,283 km2 (328 cells): the 1534 outline again. Min Bin died 11 January 1554; Min Phalaung held a strong garrison at Chittagong and 'retook it without a fight' after a governor's rebellion on 19 November 1586; no loss is dated in 1552-1563.

76,559 km2: Cliopatria removes 88 cells (Chin Hills and Magwe edge, lon 92.7-94.3, lat 21.1-23.1) in 1564, now inside the Toungoo shape. Unverified for those hill cells: no page opened places a frontier there; the Bayinnaung page (read for Lan Xang) puts his empire's edge at 'the borders of Arakan'. The Arakan plain, Chittagong and Sandoway stay. The Toungoo capture of Thandwe in September 1580 is a ledger occupation.

76,861 km2: two cells more than 1564-1587. Valid to 1665: Chittagong falls to the Mughals on 27 January 1666 ('Anderkilla ... fell after a three-day siege'), so the shape does not hold for 1666-1669 as Cliopatria draws it. The Mrauk U and Razagyi pages date the Lower Burmese conquest to 1599-1603 (ledger occupations), no change of outline.

New keyframe 1666-1669: Cliopatria's 1670 outline (58,855 km2, 189 cells) four years earlier. 'On 27 January 1666 AD' Buzurg Umed Khan's Mughal forces took Chittagong; the Mughal border afterwards is the Naf River on one passage and the Kaladan on another (the page does not reconcile them).

correction.text: Arakan without Chittagong from the Mughal conquest of 27 January 1666

keyframe_review.note: 58,855 km2 (189 cells): Arakan proper without Chittagong. The page on the Mughal conquest says Arakan 'tried hard to recapture this region of Bengal' without success; none of the pages opened dates a border change in 1670-1740.
59,160 km2: the 1670 outline (+3 -1 cells on the Ava/Prome edge). The Mrauk U page is silent on 1741-1784 apart from the 1784-85 conquest.
59,214 km2: the same outline as 1741 (+1 -1 cell).
58,855 km2: the same outline as 1670-1740 (-2 cells).

58,855 km2, 189 cells. The Konbaung invasion 'commenced on December 2, 1784', the Burmese reached Laungkyet on 31 December 1784 and took Mrauk-U 'on January 2, 1785, effectively ending nearly five centuries of Arakanese independence'; Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1787 and gives the cells to its Konbaung row from 1788. The shape holds for 1783-1784 only.

ledger.note: April 1429: Min Saw Mon is proclaimed king at Launggyet, founding the Arakanese kingdom of Mrauk U. He was 'proclaimed king at Launggyet on 18 April 1429' after a February-March invasion with Bengal's help, 'as a vassal of sultanate for some time'; the Mrauk U lead gives 1429, the Bengal page 1430, and only the Inzauk Razawin chronicle 1430.

region.text: northern Arakan, 'still restricted to northern Arakan' (Min Saw Mon page); Sandoway stayed independent

ledger.note: 1431: Mrauk-U is declared the capital. 'declared the capital of the Arakanese kingdom in 1431' (Mrauk U body); the infobox gives 1430, and the Min Saw Mon page has the city founded 16 November 1430 and completed in 1432/33.
1437: Min Khayi annexes Sandoway. 'Min Khayi annexed Sandoway and Ramu in 1437.' The Min Saw Mon page has Sandoway independent until then.
1437: Min Khayi annexes Ramu. Same sentence; whose Ramu was is my reading (the Bengal Sultanate, to which the Mrauk U lead makes Arakan a protectorate).

1459: Arakan conquers Chittagong. Infobox 'Conquest of Chittagong: 1459'; the body credits Ba Saw Phyu without a year; the Bengal Sultanate page: 'A war with Arakan in 1459 led to the defeat of Bengali Sultan Rukunuddin Barbak Shah' and 'the Kingdom of Mrauk U conquered Chittagong'.

region.text: Chittagong and the hills above it (the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1534)

ledger.note: 1516: Bengal recovers Chittagong. 'Hussain Shah restored Bengali sovereignty in Chittagong and northern Arakan after the war of 1512-1516' (the infobox lists 'Conquest of Chittagong 1512-1516'). The year is the war's end; no Arakanese page records the loss, and 'northern Arakan' is not drawn.

region.text: Chittagong and the hills above it (the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1534)

ledger.note: October 1532: Min Bin retakes Chittagong. The invasion began 7 October 1532 and 'defeated a Bengal army of 10,000 men and took Chittagong'; the Mrauk U body has him seize it in the late 1530s, with a 1542 inscription.

region.text: Chittagong and the hills above it (the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1534)

ledger.note: 11 December 1532: Arakanese forces enter Dhaka. They entered 'without a fight' after the Bengal army's last stand outside the city was defeated; on 8 February 1533 he received tribute from Bengali lords.

13 April 1533: Min Bin leaves Dhaka for Mrauk-U. On 14 May 1533 he appointed governors of the new territories, but 'his control of Bengal beyond Chittagong was largely nominal'; 5,000 troops had been sent to Dhaka against Tripuri raids.

28 October 1546: Toungoo invades Arakan by land and sea with about 19,000 men, taking Thandwe; Mrauk-U is surrounded on 24 January 1547 and the siege fails. The Mrauk U page has Tabinshwehti 'invaded and took Sandoway' in 1544, the Min Bin page an intrusion driven out near Thandwe on 12 October 1545.
26 March 1547: Toungoo evacuates Thandwe. Tabinshwehti agreed a truce on 30 January 1547 and began the retreat on 2 February; the page does not say Toungoo took Mrauk-U.
9 September 1580: a Toungoo force of 24,000 under Bayinnaung's son Thiri Thudhamma Yaza 'quickly seized Thandwe'; it laid siege to Mrauk-U for over a year without breaking the fort.
November 1581: the invasion is called off after Bayinnaung's death in November 1581. The page does not say whether or when Arakan recovered Thandwe, so the end is the withdrawal.

March 1599: Arakanese ships seize Syriam. The force left Mrauk-U on 10 November 1598; Razagyi allied with the rebel Minye Thihathu of Toungoo in 1597. Filipe de Brito e Nicote was left in the Syriam garrison and made governor in June 1600.

region.text: Syriam (Thanlyin), seized by Arakanese ships in March 1599

ledger.note: December 1599: Pegu surrenders to the Arakanese. 'the siege of Pegu ended in December 1599 when Nanda surrendered' (the page gives the sequence rather than the year).

About March 1600: the Arakanese leave Pegu. After the rebel Toungoo forces left with their loot on 15 February 1600 the Arakanese remained about another month, then burned the city and deported 3,000 households; the page gives no end date.

March 1603: De Brito revolts at Syriam and the Lower Burmese coast is lost. 'De Brito revolted in March 1603 with support from the Portuguese viceroy of Goa'; the lead says the kingdom lost the Lower Burmese coastline in 1603. Between 1600 and 1603 it held over 1,600 km of coast from the Sundarbans to the Gulf of Martaban.

region.text: Syriam (Thanlyin), seized by Arakanese ships in March 1599

ledger.note: 1605: Sandwip retaken from the Portuguese. Razagyi took 'three years (1602-1605)' to retake Sandwip from the Portuguese; (Kingdom of Mrauk U page; the Min Razagyi page has no 1602-1605 Sandwip passage and starts with Tibao's seizure of 1609); the page does not say which Portuguese held it before. [reviewer se-01-f]
1609: Sebastian Gonzales Tibao seizes Sandwip. He 'returned with 400 Portuguese and seized Sandwip', 'a major loss'; in 1610 he broke the alliance and seized the Arakanese fleet.

27 January 1666: the Mughals take Chittagong. 'On 27 January 1666 AD' Buzurg Umed Khan's forces took Anderkilla, 'the Arakanese centre in the region', after a three-day siege; Sandwip fell to Abul Hasan in November 1665 (it was Dilawar's, not Arakan's). Cliopatria dates the loss 1670.

region.text: Chittagong, 'Anderkilla, the Arakanese centre in the region' (the 56 cells Cliopatria removes in 1670)

ledger.note: 2 January 1785: Konbaung armies take Mrauk-U. Thado Minsaw's force of over 20,000 reached Laungkyet on 31 December 1784; King Thamada 'was soundly defeated' and the capital fell on 2 January 1785, 'effectively ending nearly five centuries of Arakanese independence'.
2 January 1785: the Kingdom of Mrauk U ends. Infobox 'End of kingdom: 2 January 1785'; the page says it 'was conquered by the Konbaung dynasty'.

region.text: the whole kingdom, to the Konbaung dynasty

wars.name: Bengal-Arakan war of 1459

zones.text: Chittagong and the hills above it (the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1534)

wars.outcome: 'A war with Arakan in 1459 led to the defeat of Bengali Sultan Rukunuddin Barbak Shah'; Arakan holds Chittagong until 1516 (infobox: conquest of Chittagong 1459).
wars.note: The Bengal page does not say who gained Chittagong in the war; the Mrauk U infobox does.

wars.name: Bengal-Arakan war of 1512-1516

zones.text: Chittagong and the hills above it (the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1534)

wars.outcome: Hussain Shah 'restored Bengali sovereignty in Chittagong and northern Arakan'; Chittagong leaves the Arakanese outline in 1516.

wars.name: Arakanese invasion of Bengal

zones.text: Chittagong and the hills above it (the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1534)

wars.outcome: Min Bin takes Chittagong (October 1532) and enters Dhaka (11 December 1532), leaving on 13 April 1533; his control beyond Chittagong was 'largely nominal'.

wars.name: Toungoo invasion of Arakan (1545-1547)
wars.outcome: Toungoo took Thandwe and besieged Mrauk-U (24-30 January 1547) but was flooded out; truce 30 January, retreat 2 February, Thandwe evacuated 26 March 1547.

wars.name: Arakanese-Tripuran wars
wars.outcome: Tripura 'agreed to pay tribute' after its capital fell in January 1575; it joined the Chittagong rebellion of 1586 and submitted again 'within two weeks'; by February 1596 Razagyi had 'reestablished control over Tripura'.
wars.note: No vassal events: the pages give neither the end of the tribute nor the land. The Twipra Kingdom page is silent on Arakan's invasions and tribute.

wars.name: Toungoo invasion of Arakan (1580-1581)
wars.outcome: Toungoo seized Thandwe on 9 September 1580 and besieged Mrauk-U for over a year; the invasion was 'called off after Bayinnaung died in November 1581'.

wars.name: Arakanese conquest of Lower Burma

zones.text: Syriam (Thanlyin), seized by Arakanese ships in March 1599

wars.outcome: Syriam seized in March 1599, Pegu surrendered in December 1599 and was burned about March 1600; De Brito revolted at Syriam in March 1603 and the Lower Burmese coast was lost.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Chittagong

zones.text: Chittagong, 'Anderkilla, the Arakanese centre in the region' (the 56 cells Cliopatria removes in 1670)

wars.outcome: Sandwip fell in November 1665 and Anderkilla on 27 January 1666; Chittagong became a Mughal faujdar's seat.
wars.note: The border afterwards is the Naf River on one passage and the Kaladan on another; the page does not reconcile them.

wars.name: Konbaung conquest of Arakan
wars.outcome: Thado Minsaw's army of over 20,000 took Mrauk-U on 2 January 1785 and ended the kingdom; about 35,000 Rakhine fled to British Bengal.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty frontier appears on any page opened; the Naf/Kaladan line after 1666 is given two ways. The Arakan Yoma edge and Chittagong are approximate throughout.

notes: Cliopatria's shapes are close to the pages for Arakan proper (about 58,900-84,600 km2, 189-281 cells) and wrong where they move: 1547-1551 (159 cells to Toungoo, which the Min Bin page contradicts), 1670 for the loss of Chittagong (27 January 1666), 1788 for the Konbaung conquest (2 January 1785), and the absence of Chittagong in 1459-1515 and from October 1532. The Mrauk U page gives no area, so no infobox ratio exists. Disagreements: Chittagong is 1459 (infobox), 'late 1530s' (body) and 1532 (Min Bin) on three passages; the Bengal Sultanate page has Bengal take it back in 1512-1516, which no Arakanese page records; the capital is 1430 (infobox), 1431 (body) and 1432/33 (Min Saw Mon); the founding is 1429 (Mrauk U lead, Min Saw Mon) or 1430 (Bengal page); Toungoo took Sandoway in 1544 (Mrauk U) or an intrusion was driven out in October 1545 (Min Bin). Not on the pages and left out: the Bengal protectorate (the Mrauk U lead 1429-1531, the infobox 1429-1437) is carried by the Sultanate of Bengal's dossier, not here (a vassal has no event of its own); Tripura's tribute from January 1575 has no end date on any page; Dhaka's status after April 1533; the 1593 appointment of Thado Minsaw as King of Bengal with Chittagong, Noakhali and Tippera; Noakhali and Bhulua (not on the pages); the Chin Hills frontier removed in 1564 (unverified); 1670-1784 (the pages are silent); no ruler list was opened. Counterparts: sultanate-of-bengal (Cliopatria slug), first-toungoo-empire (se-01, not yet written when this was done), konbaung-dynasty (se-01), mughal-empire (sa-05); named without a slug: Launggyet's Pegu nominee, Sandoway, Tripura, Portuguese Sandwip and Syriam (De Brito).
